God Damnn Jimmy! 

Quentin Tarantino's frequent use of the N-word in Pulp Fiction and other films has long drawn industry debate and public criticism.The racial slur appears 13 times in Pulp Fiction, notably during the "Bonnie Situation" sequence where Tarantino’s character, Jimmie, aggressively uses the term while talking to Jules (Samuel L. Jackson) and Vincent (John Travolta). However, Tarantino and defenders of his work, including Samuel L. Jackson, have argued that the language is meant to reflect raw character realism, distinct conversational contexts, and the gritty, unvarnished speech patterns of his fictional settings rather than gratuitous malice.

source_details.synopsis: Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary. It tells four intertwining tales of crime and violence in Los Angeles. The film stars John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis, Tim Roth, Ving Rhames, and Uma Thurman. The title refers to the pulp magazines and hardboiled crime novels popular during the mid-twentieth century, known for their graphic violence and punchy dialogue. Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction in 1992 and 1993, incorporating scenes that Avary originally wrote for True Romance (1993). Its plot occurs out of chronological order.
